siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

resident_assignment.note: NO KEEPER, AND NOT FOR WANT OF ONE (T-1691). The placement policy's platted deal seated a household on this roof under its tradesman_dwellings clause, on blk_west_lake_des_plaines#00 — a standing anonymous roof of family D3 that clause admits — and T-1691 refused to carry it onto the record: a household minted from the post office's letter lists, which the owner's ruling of 2026-08-30 (T-0379) refuses a roof: a letter-list name is a name the town knows, not a man with an address. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py --gate holds it. The placement policy's deal seated this household here anyway, and that disagreement is the deal's to answer, not this pass's to route around. The seat still stands in data/reconstruction/1835_platted_seats.json and the refusal in data/reconstruction/1835_roof_keepers.json § refused, which names the household; this note deliberately does not, because naming it here is the claim the ruling forbids. WHETHER THAT IS A SHORTAGE, MEASURED: 44 unseated household(s) of this same clause and division carry a source for their name and are refused a roof by no ruling (1835_roof_keepers.json § households_left, re-derived from the deal's own owed rows on every commit). So the roof stands empty because the deal does not consult the ruling before it deals, not because the town ran out of people. The roof itself is unchanged: a conjectural count-unit of the 665-roof programme, adopted by nobody, its existence, position and footprint as invented as before.
